n: Israel speaks as one person looking back on its history: since its ‘youth’ in Egypt, enemies have attacked it again and again. The leader invites the people to say it together.

f.g: From Israel’s beginnings as a nation, in Egypt.

n: Yet for all their attacks, the enemies have never defeated Israel. God’s covenant people survive.

f.w: they have not prevailed against me

n: A vivid image of cruelty: enemies dragged plows across Israel’s back, cutting long furrows — like the welts of a whipping.

f.w: The plowers plowed upon my back

n: But the righteous Lord cut the ropes that harnessed Israel to the plow — he set his people free.

f.w: cut asunder the cords of the wicked

n: A prayer that all who hate Zion will be put to shame and driven back.

f.g: Put to shame, thrown into confusion.

n: May they be like grass sprouting on a flat clay rooftop — it springs up but withers quickly with no deep soil.

f.g: Flat mud roofs sprouted thin grass that soon dried up.

n: Such grass is useless: a reaper can’t gather even a handful, nor a binder an armful.
No passerby will offer the usual harvest greeting, ‘The Lord bless you!’ — as Boaz and his workers greeted each other.

f.w: The blessing of the LORD be upon you
